facts: The principal question of law which arises in this group of 37 civil appeals relates to the construction of section 3 of the Madras Essential Articles Control and Requisitioning (Temporary Powers) Act, 1949.

The dispute which has given rise to these appeals centres round the validity of two notified orders issued by the respondent, State of Andhra Pradesh on the 28th January, 1955, and30th January, 1955 respectively,
issues: Construction of section 3 of the Madras Essential Articles Control and Requisitioning (Temporary Powers) Act, 1949
Validity of two notified orders issued by the respondent, State of Andhra Pradesh
petitioner_arguments: Section 3 does not confer power on the respondent to enhance the tariff rate chargeable against the appellants in respect of the supply of energy made by the respondent to them.

The whole scheme of the Act indicates clearly that the power to regulate the supply of an essential article which has been conferred on the State Government has to be applied in regard to transaction between citizens and citizens and cannot be applied to an essential article: which the State itself supplies.
respondent_arguments: On its fair and reasonable construction, s. 3 does confer authority on the respondent to issue the impugned orders
The main reason which inspired the said orders was the knowledge that the existing electricity tariffs which were formulated nearly 15 years before, had become completely uneconomic
court_reasoning: Before addressing ourselves to the question of construing s. 3, it is necessary to recapitulate the legislative history of the Act.
The rule of harmonious construction requires that we must construe all the provisions of the Act as to avoid any conflict or repugnancy between them.
holding: The impugned orders are outside the purview of s. 3 and are therefore invalid
